reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Grading from imaging alone without the operative description.
name: Simpson Grade of Meningioma Resection

version.label: Simpson (1957), grades I–V
version.detail: Extent of meningioma resection as judged by the surgeon. Grade 0 (resection with a dural margin) is a later proposal and is not combined.

purpose: Describes the extent of meningioma resection.

options.label: Grade I: Macroscopically complete removal, including the dural attachment and any abnormal bone
Grade II: Macroscopically complete removal with coagulation of the dural attachment
Grade III: Macroscopically complete removal without resection or coagulation of the dural attachment or extradural extensions
Grade V: Simple decompression, with or without biopsy

resultStates.label: Grade I
resultStates.summary: Macroscopically complete removal, including the dural attachment and any abnormal bone.
resultStates.detail: Recurrence: 9% symptomatic recurrence at 10 years in Simpson's series.

resultStates.label: Grade II
resultStates.summary: Macroscopically complete removal with coagulation of the dural attachment.

resultStates.label: Grade III
resultStates.summary: Macroscopically complete removal without resection or coagulation of the dural attachment or extradural extensions.

resultStates.label: Grade V
resultStates.summary: Simple decompression, with or without biopsy.
resultStates.detail: Recurrence: High recurrence (small group in the original series).

clinicalContext.text: Extent of resection is a key predictor of meningioma recurrence; the 1957 series showed rising recurrence with grade.

clinicalInsights.text: Modern series find smaller differences between grades I–III; WHO grade and location also matter.

limitations: Recurrence figures come from a 1957 single-surgeon series.
whatItDoesNotTellYou: Need for adjuvant treatment on its own.

guideSections.whenToUse: Operative notes and follow-up planning after meningioma surgery.
guideSections.howToPerform: From the operative findings, record removal of tumour, dura and bone; choose the grade.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with WHO grade, MRI and location.

sources.citation: Simpson D. The recurrence of intracranial meningiomas after surgical treatment. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 1957;20(1):22-39.
